# driftwatch spool

The spool is the durable buffer between ingest and the exporter. Every
accepted batch lands in the spool before the ingest response is sent,
so an accepted write survives a crash or an exporter outage.

## Layout

Spool data lives under the data directory as numbered segment files.
Segments are append-only; a segment that has rolled is immutable and
is eligible for retention sweeps once exported.

## Pacing

Buffered batches drain to the active segment on a fixed cadence. The
shipped default flushes twice a minute; deployments tune this per
profile through the config layer. Lowering the cadence smooths disk
pressure at the cost of a slightly larger replay window after a crash.

## Sizing

Keep the spool on local disk, not network storage. Size it for at
least a day of peak ingest so an exporter outage over a weekend does
not force retention sweeps to run early.

# driftwatch alerting

Alert rules live in the rules directory and hot-reload on change. Each
rule names an expression, a hold window, and a severity; transitions
out of pending are what page.

## Routing

Fired alerts post to a chat webhook. The destination channel and the
webhook token are deployment config: routing is an operator decision,
not a code default, and teams point different severities at different
rooms as they see fit.

## Hygiene

Keep rule expressions cheap; the evaluation loop walks every rule on
each tick and a slow query delays the whole pass. Pre-declare planned
maintenance in the ops calendar so silences are visible ahead of time
and paging stays quiet during planned work.

## Reviewing

Rule changes go through the fortnightly ops sync. Bring a graph of the
expression over at least a week of history so hold windows are tuned
against real flap behaviour rather than a single incident.

# driftwatch operations

driftwatch ships as a single static binary. Run it under a process
supervisor with the spool on local disk, and point producers at a
stable DNS name rather than an address.

## Restarts

Send SIGTERM and wait. Ingest stops accepting, the spool drains for a
bounded grace period, and anything still buffered is picked up on the
next start. No manual intervention is required.

## Credential rotation

Rotations are staged through config: add the incoming credential shape
to the accepted set, migrate producers, then narrow the accepted set
again once the drain completes. Never narrow first; producers signing
with retired credentials are rejected at the edge.

## Tenants

Per-tenant ingest budgets live in the tenants file and hot-reload on
change. Prefer explicit entries for every production tenant; the
built-in default exists for evaluation, not for steady state.

# driftwatch replay

Replay re-reads rolled spool segments and hands them to the exporter.
It exists for exporter outages and for backfills after a schema
change; it never touches the active segment, so ingest keeps running
while a replay is in flight.

## Running a replay

Start the daemon with the replay subcommand and a segment range, or
omit the range to resume from the checkpoint. Progress is
checkpointed continuously, so an interrupted replay resumes where it
left off rather than re-reading from the start.

## Drills

Run the monthly drill against staging with a bounded range first.
Watch the exporter lag panel during the drill; replay deliberately
yields to live ingest when the exporter falls behind, so a slow drill
is usually a sign of exporter pressure, not replay trouble.

# driftwatch alerting

Alert rules live in the rules directory and hot-reload on change. Each
rule names an expression, a hold window, and a severity; transitions
out of pending are what page.

## Repeat notifications

A rule that keeps firing does not page continuously. Repeat
notifications are held back by a debounce; the shipped default lives
in the alert engine and individual rules may override it in the rules
file when a signal needs faster or slower repeats.

## Routing

Fired alerts post to a chat webhook. The destination channel and the
webhook token are deployment config, and delivery failures park in a
retry queue that drains automatically after an outage.

## Reviewing

Rule changes go through the fortnightly ops sync. Bring history with
the proposal so hold windows and debounce overrides are tuned against
real flap behaviour rather than a single incident.

# driftwatch export

The exporter walks rolled spool segments and writes parquet shards for
the warehouse. Shards are the unit of retry and of loader
parallelism, so their sizing is a contract with the warehouse team as
much as a local tuning knob.

## Scheduling

Export runs are cron-driven from deployment config. Pick the window
against the warehouse maintenance calendar; the exporter skips a run
that would overlap the previous one rather than stacking load on a
warehouse that is already behind.

## Failure handling

A failed shard retries independently; a failed run resumes from the
last completed shard on the next trigger. Watch the run-failure and
overlap-skip counters after any schedule change.

# driftwatch spool

The spool is the durable buffer between ingest and the exporter. Every
accepted batch lands in the spool before the ingest response is sent,
so an accepted write survives a crash or an exporter outage.

## Layout

Spool data lives under the data directory as numbered segment files.
Segments are append-only; a segment that has rolled is immutable and
is eligible for retention sweeps once exported.

## Sizing and backpressure

The spool has a per-node size ceiling; at the ceiling, ingest applies
backpressure instead of eating the volume. Size the underlying disk
with headroom above the ceiling so segment rollover and replay
working space never compete with live ingest for the last bytes.
rag_sources.abstract: Spool guide: durable buffer role, segment layout, ceiling and backpressure.
rag_sources.overview: spool.md explains the spool's durable-buffer role, the numbered segment layout, and the per-node ceiling with ingest backpressure, plus disk headroom guidance.

# driftwatch alerting

Alert rules live in the rules directory and hot-reload on change.
Transitions out of pending are what page; the delivery path from a
firing rule to a human runs through the fanout pool and the notifier.

## Delivery

Fired alerts fan out through a fixed worker pool to the notifier.
Pool sizing is a code constant tuned against load tests, not runtime
config: delivery capacity is a property the team reasons about at
review time, and silent config drift here would be a paging outage
waiting to happen.

## Failure handling

Delivery failures park in a bounded retry queue that drains
automatically with backoff. Watch the dropped-entry counter after any
long chat outage; a nonzero value means the outage outlived the
queue's memory.

rag_sources.content:
# driftwatch retention

Retention manages rolled spool segments across the warm and cold
tiers and deletes what has aged out of both. Keep durations are
deployment config; the sweep machinery and its pacing are code.

## Sweeps

The sweeper makes regular passes over every tier. Passes are spaced
so a slow volume cannot pile up concurrent sweeps: a pass that would
overlap a still-running one is deferred, and the deferral shows up in
the pass logs rather than in a stuck queue.

## Safety

A segment is only ever swept after the exporter's watermark has
passed it, so retention can never delete data the warehouse has not
seen. If sweeps and exports fight over io, cap the sweep io on the
cold volume rather than widening the sweep spacing.

rag_sources.overview: retention.md explains the warm and cold tier model with config-driven keep durations, deferred (never stacked) sweep passes, and the export watermark rule that keeps deletion behind the warehouse.

# driftwatch tenants

Every producer maps to a tenant, and every tenant maps to a stanza in
the tenants file: an ingest rate, a burst allowance, and the team and
cost-center tags the capacity reports group by.

## Changing a rate

Rate changes are config deploys. Edit the stanza, let the lint pass,
and the hot reload applies it without a restart; the limiter picks up
the new rate on its next refill tick. Keep the change and its
rationale in the commit message, because the capacity summary links
stanza history when quotas are questioned.

## Defaults

Tenants the file does not name get the conservative built-in default.
That default is for evaluation traffic only; production tenants get
explicit stanzas, reviewed with the team tag owner.
